scope: Independent first-party text/structured design review only. This is not executable-source, API, lifecycle, runtime, scientific or physical validation and grants no implementation or operation authority.

original_findings_preserved.issue: Original U1/ownership invariants suppress only the leader default destructor. Native and fixed-query handles can remain unreaped at110, so their default destructor/release paths were not specified.
original_findings_preserved.resolution: Require the additive all-owned-handle rule, including partial construction, strong retention, no inherited destructor or active-list cleanup fallback, explicit exact-PID reap only, and no child-state API after110. Constructor internal work and process-wide cleanup behavior remain source-proof obligations.

original_findings_preserved.issue: Original caller table has no successful NATIVE_IDENTITY to NATIVE_RUNNING edge.
original_findings_preserved.resolution: Require the additive edge only for timely matching retained PID/caller PPID/certified PGID and valid clock joins with no stop/error. Failure, stop, equality/late deadline and incomplete identity retain precedence.

important_limits: Private no-op destructor is a future fixed local source obligation, not proof that constructor internals cannot run late, create unknown children or enter process-wide cleanup.
Outer cannot reap a native/query grandchild; unavailable or unconsumed terminal status at110 remains unknown/unreaped. Teardown is never credited as reap, group absence or receipt completion.
Complete-candidate receipts do not predict their own final size, hash, raw return status or whole startup-through-return time. Independent final postwrite/outer-return observations remain mandatory.

Native100 and TERM10 are preserved upper limits;95/105/110/115 reservations add control boundaries without changing material, geometry, loads, tolerances, solver arguments, force gates or numerical thresholds.
No containment, runtime/provider equivalence, sampled true peak, ABI, native solve, head feasibility or physical/manufacturing qualification follows.
